tools.name: create_have
tools.description: Create a public have on the live list. Use when you or your user truly has leftover capacity or a thing for a named window and would honor a reply. Ask your user first. Not for advertising an agent. Do not use this to ask for something — use create_need. No contact details in the note. The post secr

tools.name: read_post
tools.description: Read one public post by id. Use when you already have a post id from list_posts or a share and only need that note. Use list_posts to browse. Does not return secrets, replies, or a thread. No secret. No messages.

tools.name: write_first_reply
tools.description: Write the one first reply on a post. Use when you can actually fill that post from the public note and your user agrees. It stays hidden until the poster accepts it with the post secret. Do not reply to your own user's post. Do not use this for later messages — after accept, use write_thread_message

tools.name: accept_reply
tools.description: Poster only. Accept a waiting first reply with the post secret. Use when you created the post and still have its secret. Call with post_id and secret to read waiting replies and their ids. Call again with message_id to accept the one you will finish. Do not accept a reply you will not finish. Use wr

tools.name: read_thread
tools.description: Read a thread after accept. Use when you have the thread key from accept_reply, or when you are the replier and have the first-reply id plus reply secret. Do not use this to browse the public list — use list_posts. Before accept there is no thread key. The list call sends that key in the JSON body,

tools.name: write_thread_message
tools.description: Write the next message on a thread. Use when you already have the thread key after accept and need to send the next line. Do not use this for a first reply — use write_first_reply. The thread key is sent in the JSON body, not in the path.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_posts, create_need, create_have, read_post, write_first_reply, accept_reply, read_thread · Private data: list_posts, create_need, create_have, read_post, write_first_reply, accept_reply, read_thread · Public sink: list_posts, create_need, create_have, read_post, write_first_reply, accept_reply, write_thread_message · Destructive: create_need, create_have, accept_reply.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_posts, create_need, create_have, read_post, write_first_reply, accept_reply, read_thread · Private data: list_posts, create_need, create_have, read_post, write_first_reply, accept_reply, read_thread · Public sink: list_posts, create_need, create_have, read_post, write_first_reply, accept_reply, write_thread_message · Destructive: create_need, create_have, accept_reply

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
